texts.preamble: M/S Nirma Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 August, 2018 1 M.Cr.C.No.10660 of 2012 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Principal Seat At Jabalpur Single Bench : Hon'ble Shri Rajeev Kumar Dubey, J. Misc. Criminal Case No.10660/2012 M/s. Nirma Limited & Anr. vs. State of M.P. & Anr. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Shri Manikant Sharma, counsel for the applicants. Shri Akhilendra Singh, Govt. Advocate for the respondents/State. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Order
texts.facts: This petition has been filed under Section 482 of CrPC against the order dated 13.08.2012 passed by Sessions Judge, Narsinghpur in Cr.R.No.83/2012 whereby he rejected the applicants' revision and affirmed the order dated 03.07.2012 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Narsinghpur in Criminal Case No.31/2011. Brief facts of the case which are relevant for just disposal of the present case are that on 07.07.2009 complainant, Food Inspector Sarika Choubey inspected the applicants/accused shop situated at Radha Vallabh Ward, Kareli, District Narsinghpur and took the sample of one packet of Nirma Pure Salt and sent it to Public Analyst who gave report that salt had been adulterated. On that, written complaint against the applicants was filed on 07/01/11 and learned JMFC took cognizance against the applicants for the offence punishable under Section 7 (1) r/w 16 (1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'). Applicants appeared before the trial Court on 13.01.2011 and filed an application under section 13(2) of the Act for sending second part of the sample of salt to Central Food Laboratory for re examination. Learned Trial Court allowed that application by order dated 20.04.2012 and directed that second part of the sample be sent to Central Food Laboratory Ghaziabad for re examination on depositing draft of analysis fee by the applicant. Applicant instead of depositing draft of analysis fee for sending second part of sample for analysis filed an application before trial court on 28/06/12 that the sample becomes unfit for analysis after expiry date of the sample. Hence, the valuable right of the applicant given under Section 13 (2) of the Act is affected. So the criminal proceedings pending against applicant be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. M/S Nirma Limited vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193531852/ 1 Learned trial court rejected the application filed by the applicants on 03.07.2012 observing that just because it was mentioned on the sample that it was best for use only till two years from the date of its production, it cannot be said that the sample becomes unfit for analysis. It could only be decided by the CFL. Against this the applicants filed revision which too was dismissed by learned Sessions Judge vide order dated 13.08.2018 observing that impugned order is an interim order against which revision is not maintainable. Being aggrieved from that order, applicants filed this petition. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that salt packet in question was best for use only till two years from the date of its production as printed on the packet. The sample was taken on 07.07.2009 and complaint was filed by the complainant/non applicant before court on 07/01/11. Applicant filed the application under section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act on 13.01.2011 well within time. But prosecution took long time to file reply of that application and did not file reply up to 20/04/12. In the meantime, shelf life of sample expired and sample became unfit for analysis. The applicant could only exercise his right under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act within two years from the production of the sample i.e., 06/07/11. After lapse of that period the sample was no longer in the food category. Hence, the applicants' right given under Section 13 (2) of Act to re- analyze his sample has been violated. So, the proceedings be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned trial court as well as learned revisional court committed mistake in rejecting applicant's application.
texts.arguments: In this regard, learned counsel for the applicants also placed reliance on the Apex Court judgment passed in the case of Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah vs. C.C. Jani & Another reported in (2009) 15 SCC 64 and State of Haryana vs. Unique Farmaid (P) Ltd. & Ors. reported in (1999) 8 SCC 190. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and submitted that the second part of the sample is yet to be analysed by the Central Food Laboratory without which it cannot be said that the accused has been denied of his right to get the second part of the sample analysed by the Central Food Testing Laboratory. The applicant deliberately filed this petition with the intent to prolong the case and also got a stay, due to which the proceedings of the case in the Trial Court have stopped. So only on the ground of delay, the proceedings of the trial cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Apex Court in the case of Ajit Prasad Ram Krishna Singh v. State of Maharashtra reported in 1972 FAC 545 observed as thus: "It is clear from the sub-section that the appellant should have made an application after paying the prescribed fee if he wanted the part of the sample available with him to be sent to the Director for analysis. In Babulal Hargovindas v. State of Gujarat Jaganmohan Reddy, J. speaking for the Court, said that unless an application to send the sample to the Director is made, the vendor cannot complain that he was deprived of his right to have the sample analysed by the Director".
